topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and states its learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of cancer susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arise and enable susceptible cells to evolve into cancer within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and the evidence for their importance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contribution of environmental exposures to cancer risk and how that contribution is interpreted from observed cancer patterns.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example of cooperating infectious influences.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage that can become cancer-driving mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how tumour promoters enable the outgrowth of initiated cells without necessarily acting as direct mutagens.

topics.label: Developmental susceptibility and recap of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics complete the account of context-dependent carcinogenesis by explaining developmental susceptibility and recapping the mechanisms already discussed.

topics.label: Mutational signatures as evidence of carcinogen exposure
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how patterns in cancer genomes can provide retrospective evidence of exposure to particular carcinogens.

topics.label: Methods and limitations of carcinogenicity assessment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how carcinogenic potential can be assessed and why the available methods cannot fully reproduce or establish human cancer risk.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and framing everyday exposure decisions as balances of risks and benefits.
